h1: The 5 Best 24-Inch Monitor Privacy Screens of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 5 best 24 inch monitor privacy screens, from 3M optical film to magnetic 2-packs, compared on attachment and price.
summary: The 3M filter with Comply magnetic attachment is the best 24 inch privacy screen for one monitor, because it names its film and pops off quickly. The 3M widescreen model keeps the optical film without a stated mount. Dual desks should choose the Peslv pair, or the magnetic 2-pack for frequent sharing.
intro: Put five 24 inch privacy filters side by side and they look like the same sheet of dark plastic. The difference shows up later, in the film behind the logo and in how the filter comes off. A filter that is fiddly to remove tends to stay on during every presentation, and then colleagues squint at your screen from a metre away and ask you to take it off.

We ranked five filters, all cut for 16:9 panels, on film brand, attachment, pack size and price bucket. Two are from 3M, which names its optical film, while the rest state size and count and little else. Because brightness and angle figures are not in our data, we judge on documented build and convenience, not optical claims.

products.name: 3M Privacy Filter for 24in Full Screen Monitor with 3M Comply Magnetic Attach
products.verdict: 3M filter with a magnetic attachment you can pop off.
products.description:
The 3M Comply filter is a 24 inch, 16:9 full-screen filter with a magnetic attachment, in the $50 to $100 bucket. Two things stand out. The film is branded, so you know whose optics you are looking through, and the Comply mount lets the filter lift off with a pull and return without adhesive. That combination is what turns a privacy filter from a one-time install into something you actually take off.

It ranks first because the sibling 3M model lists the film but not the mount, and the generic packs list neither a film nor a proven magnet system. Only this one covers both brand and quick removal.

Buy it for a single desk where you share your screen sometimes. The caveat is quantity: it covers one monitor, so a dual setup needs two purchases.
products.idealFor: Single-monitor desks that share their screen.
products.skipIf: You need two filters in one buy.

products.name: 3M Privacy Filters for 24 Inch Widescreen Monitor, 16:9 Aspect Ratio
products.verdict: Genuine 3M optical film for a 24 inch widescreen.
products.description:
The second 3M filter fits 24 inch, 16:9 widescreen monitors and lists genuine 3M optical film, in the $50 to $100 bucket. Optical film is the working part of any privacy filter, and a named maker means a known source rather than an anonymous sheet. For buyers who care about the film itself, that is the main reason to pay this tier.

It ranks behind the Comply model for a plain reason: the listing does not state an attachment method. You know the film, but you do not know how quickly it comes off, and removal speed decides whether you use the privacy feature in meetings.

Buy it if you value the film brand and rarely change your screen's state. Check the product page for how it attaches before buying. Skip it if fast removal matters, since the Comply version is built for that.
products.idealFor: Buyers who prefer branded optical film.

products.name: Peslv [2-Pack] 24 Inch Privacy Screen for Computer Monitor, 16:9 Aspect Ratio
products.verdict: Two removable 24 inch filters for a dual setup.
products.description:
The Peslv ships two removable filters for 24 inch, 16:9 monitors in the $50 to $100 bucket. Two matching filters mean both screens in a dual setup get the same treatment, and a removable design means neither is permanently stuck to a bezel.

It lands third because it gives up the 3M name. The listing does not describe the film, so you cannot judge optical quality, but you do get a second filter for a price similar to one 3M. For two-monitor desks that arithmetic is hard to ignore.

Buy it for a dual 24 inch workstation where per-screen cost matters. Skip it if you want a named optical film, because the 3M models fill that role. A single monitor leaves the second filter unused, so a one-screen desk gains nothing from the pair.
products.skipIf: You prefer a named brand film.

products.name: 2 Pack 24 Inch Magnetic Computer Privacy Screen for Monitor, 16:9 Aspect Ratio
products.verdict: Two magnetic filters if you want quick removal on two screens.
products.description:
This 2-pack uses magnetic attachment for 24 inch, 16:9 monitors, in the $50 to $100 bucket. Magnets make each filter quick to pull off for screen sharing and quick to restore, and the pack covers two screens, which matches the dual-monitor desks that share most.

It ranks fourth because the magnet system carries no brand. 3M's Comply mount is a named design, while this listing leaves magnet strength and bezel fit unconfirmed. A weak magnet can let a filter drift or fall off, and you will not know until you try.

Buy it for two monitors that you uncover often. Check the listing and owner feedback on how the magnets grip your bezel before ordering. Skip it if you want a named film or mount, which the 3M Comply model offers for a single screen.

products.name: Computer Privacy Screen Filter for 24 Inch 16:9 Aspect Ratio Monitor
products.verdict: The cheapest single 24 inch filter in this ranking.
products.description:
This unnamed single is a 24 inch, 16:9 privacy filter in the $25 to $50 bucket, the cheapest filter in the ranking. It does one thing: covers one monitor at the lowest cost.

It ranks last because the listing names no brand, no attachment and no film. That matters because every other pick tells you something about how it mounts or what it is made of. Here you get size and nothing more, so you are buying on trust. The price gap to the next product is a full bucket, and for some buyers that is enough.

Buy it for a low-cost single-monitor desk where you accept unknowns. Skip it if you share your screen regularly or want documented features. Confirm how it attaches before assuming it suits your bezel.

whatMatters.detail: The 24 inch figure is the screen diagonal and 16:9 is the shape. A filter cut for the wrong shape leaves gaps or hangs over the edge. Read your monitor's specs for the exact ratio, then match it to the listing. Every filter here is listed for 24 inch, 16:9 only, so do not assume it fits, and never trim one.

A privacy filter's film does the work, and a named optical film like 3M's has a clear source. Unnamed film is harder to judge. Look for the film name in the title or first bullet, and note whether the listing says genuine, as the second 3M model does. Brand is a proxy for consistency across the whole sheet, edge to edge.

Attachment decides how often you will use the filter. Magnetic mounts, like 3M's Comply system, snap on and off in seconds. Fixed designs stay put and are slower to remove. Pick by how often you share your screen. Look for the words magnetic or removable in the listing, and check how your bezel holds it.

Pack count sets your cost per screen. Two filters cover two monitors, while a single covers one. Buying a single when you have two means a second order and possibly mismatched tint. Count your screens, check whether the listing says 2-pack or single, and confirm each filter is the same size.

Filters run from the $25 to $50 bucket up to $50 to $100. Paying more mostly buys a named film and a convenient mount, not a larger screen. Weigh the 3M tier against the unnamed single by how often you share your screen and how much you value a named source. Check the live price on the day, since it can move.

faq.q: Will these fit a 24 inch monitor of any shape?
faq.a: They are listed for 16:9. Most 24 inch monitors are, but some use a different ratio, so read your own spec sheet. If yours does, check before buying, because the 3M, Peslv and magnetic filters are all cut for 16:9 only.

Buying a fixed filter and then leaving it on during every screen share, which annoys colleagues and defeats the purpose. A magnetic design, like the 3M Comply or the magnetic 2-pack, comes off easily, so you actually take it off when needed.

faq.q: Is 3M worth it over the generic filter?
faq.a: If you want named optical film and a magnetic mount, yes, since the Comply model delivers both. If cost matters most, the unnamed single at $25 to $50 is cheaper but says little about its build or how it attaches.

faq.q: How do I install a magnetic filter?
faq.a: Follow the listing instructions. The 3M Comply system is designed for attach and remove, and the magnetic 2-pack uses the same idea. Make sure the bezel surface is clean and dry before fitting, then press evenly along each edge.

faq.q: Can I use one on a different size?
faq.a: No. Each filter is listed for 24 inch screens only. A 27 inch monitor needs a 27 inch filter, and trimming a 24 inch one will not work. Check your diagonal and ratio before ordering any of these.

faq.q: Does the 3M widescreen filter attach magnetically?
faq.a: The listing does not say, so check the product page. The Comply model states a magnetic mount, while the widescreen 3M lists genuine optical film but gives no attachment method for the 16:9 size.

finalTake: Buy the 3M Comply magnetic filter for a single monitor you share often. Take the Peslv or the magnetic 2-pack when you run two screens, and the unnamed single only when cost is everything. Confirm that your monitor is truly 16:9 first, since every filter here is cut for that shape.
